note: The headline speed of all-optical switching is read off the femtosecond pulse duration. Write latency, pulse count, repetition-rate ceiling and thermal recovery ride along and are assumed to travel with it.

components.name: duration of a single excitation pulse
pulses needed for deterministic reversal of one region
maximum pulse rate the source and the material can sustain
time for the heated region to cool below the switching-relevant temperature between pulses
elapsed time from write command to stable reversed domain

divergences.note: The 120 fs pulse duration is the excitation width; the reversal in [Pt/Co]N is cumulative over many pulses. The ferromagnet lacks the ferrimagnetic sublattice dynamics that permit single-pulse toggle reversal, so no component of the write is actually 120 fs long.

pulse_duration.source: Khalid et al., Nat Commun 17, 10843 (2026), Methods

pulse_count.unit: pulses per illuminated area, estimated from sweep speed and 1 kHz rate
pulse_count.source: supplementary section 10 (~200 pulses per um^2 at 5 um/s) and sweep arithmetic (1 um/s over 1-2 um spots)

divergences.note: The 1 kHz repetition rate is a property of the benchtop amplifier, not of the material's thermal recovery. Even if recovery were sub-nanosecond, the term as used would still read fast because it is read off the pulse, not off the clock that gates the next pulse.
No instrument in the study measured total write time. The 1000x figure is a prospective estimate extrapolated from pulse duration; the load-bearing component of the term is the one with no reading.

write_latency.source: not measured; XenoSpectrum analysis of the study, 2026-09-28
